claims.text: An atomically thin, conformal Pt layer deposited by ALD on a high-surface-area ceria-based support will increase catalytic activity relative to conventionally impregnated Pt catalysts.
The ALD-prepared catalyst will have greater durability under automotive exhaust conditions than conventionally impregnated Pt catalysts.
The ALD intervention will reduce overall Pt usage while maintaining or improving catalyst performance.
Conventional Pt nanoparticle impregnation provides limited control over Pt dispersion.
ALD can form a uniform, ultrathin Pt coating on a high-surface-area ceria-based support.
The proposed Pt coating and ceria support constitute a core–shell structure.
The ALD-deposited Pt layer will produce high Pt dispersion.
The conformal Pt layer will improve metal–support contact.
The conformal Pt layer will minimize Pt nanoparticle coarsening.
Enhanced Pt–ceria interactions will reduce Pt sintering during high-temperature operation.
Enhanced Pt–ceria interfacial interactions will improve oxygen activation.
Improved oxygen activation at the Pt–ceria interface will increase catalytic turnover.
The ALD-prepared catalyst will exhibit higher exhaust-gas conversion rates than the conventionally impregnated catalyst.
The ALD-prepared catalyst will undergo less activity deactivation over time than the conventionally impregnated catalyst.
The predicted activity and durability improvements can be achieved with approximately 30% less Pt.
The proposed benefits should persist after approximately 100 hours of aging at about 700°C in an oxidizing and humid atmosphere.
The proposed benefits might not persist at temperatures significantly above 800°C.
